_: Campus landmarks researched 2026-08-03 (Stuart Collection pages, press, aerials) for campus-landmarks.js. Fallen Star position was independently georeferenced - Wikipedia's coordinate is ~400 m off. Colours re-measured 2026-08-03 from 4K walk (W:fNNNN) and drone (D:fNNNN) footage; every hex below is a measurement with its frame named in the description, lifted to daylight where the drone frame was overcast or dusk.

fallenStar.cornerEvidence: D:f0034-f0036. The cottage is NOT on a corner of the main block: Jacobs Hall's south face is a comb of slender concrete stair towers, and the house sits on one of them with building mass on both sides. The georeferenced point lands 3.7 m off that south face at x=546 in local metres, west of the footprint's mid-span (504..605) - south-west, agreeing with this tag. The prose in the Fallen Star landmark entry used to say 'northeast corner' and was wrong.

landmarks.name: Sun God
landmarks.description: Niki de Saint Phalle's great bird, repainted from footage. The earlier reading had the body sprayed all over with small bright blotches, and that is wrong in the way that matters: the colour arrives as a handful of very large deliberate motifs on white. Measured D:f0100-f0101 (close aerial) and W:f0059 (eye level, sunlit): WHITE body; a scarlet head with a blue crown band and a big hooked beak a shade darker and more purple than the head itself; and behind the head a gold sunburst crest of about nine tapered spikes radiating up and out in a fan. One big concentric disc on the chest (red outer ring, blue ring, gold sun-centre) and one oval target on each outstretched wing (red, green and gold rings around a blue-red core); feet and legs painted in the same red/blue/yellow/green family. It stands on a low arch that is completely blanketed in ivy - a dark green mass with an arched opening beneath it, not the bare grey concrete assumed before; only the cap the bird stands on shows pale concrete. Bird ~4.3 m over a ~4.5 m arch. Low-poly: ivy piers + ivy lintel + pale cap, white body and wings, scarlet head, gold spike fan, and coaxial ring discs that read from either side.

landmarks.name: Fallen Star
landmarks.description: Do Ho Suh's small blue New England cottage perched at a tilt on Jacobs Hall (roof ~29 m up), cantilevered over the edge as if crash-landed. Measured D:f0034-f0036: powder-blue clapboard walls, white door/window trim, grey shingle pitched roof (lighter and bluer than the near-black the file used to carry), red brick chimney. It sits on one of the slender concrete stair towers that comb the building's SOUTH face - not on a corner of the main block, which is why it has building on both sides of it in the aerials - and hangs off that tower's south-WEST corner, with the rooftop garden (lawn, shrubs, a purple-leaf tree, ivy spilling over the tower edge) filling the rest of the tower roof inboard of the house. Low-poly: simple gabled house box ~5 m tall rotated ~10 deg off the building's grid and pitched ~10 deg over the drop. The rendered spec - position, corner, tilt, dimensions and every colour - lives in the top-level fallenStar block, not here.

landmarks.name: Snake Path
landmarks.description: Alexis Smith's 171 m long, 3 m wide winding footpath shaped like a serpent, running from Warren Mall (east end 32.881275,-117.235907) up the hillside to the Geisel Library terrace (west end 32.881024,-117.237041). Surface is hexagonal slate tiles in a scale pattern: mottled green, grey, and tan. Head (with eyes) at the top near Geisel; tail at the bottom; mid-path it coils around a small walled 'Garden of Eden' with fruit trees and passes an oversized granite book. Low-poly: a flat S-curving ribbon with green/grey checker texture, slightly raised, widening to a spade-shaped head.

landmarks.name: Silent Tree
landmarks.description: Terry Allen's dead eucalyptus tree wrapped entirely in dull grey lead sheet, standing on Library Walk just south of Geisel Library. Bare branching trunk, no leaves, matte lead grey with visible panel seams - measured W:f0151, a warm-neutral gunmetal rather than a blue steel. Classic meeting spot. Low-poly: a leafless tree of 5-8 tapering cylinders, uniform lead grey.

landmarks.name: Trees (Talking Tree)
landmarks.description: Second of Terry Allen's three lead-clad eucalyptus trunks, hidden in the living eucalyptus grove southwest of Geisel; plays spoken poems and stories from concealed speakers. Same look as Silent Tree: bare grey-lead branching trunk among tall living trees. Low-poly: identical grey leafless tree, surrounded by normal green eucalyptus.

landmarks.name: Trees (Singing Tree)
landmarks.description: Third Terry Allen lead-covered eucalyptus, ~70 m west of the Talking Tree in the same grove; emits songs. Matte grey leafless trunk with lead panel seams. Low-poly: same grey tree model reused.

landmarks.name: Bear (Warren Bear)
landmarks.description: Tim Hawkinson's teddy-bear built from eight huge rounded granite boulders (~180 tons), sitting upright in the Jacobs School engineering courtyard between CSE, EBU1, and the Bioengineering building. Warm grey-tan granite, measured twice (W:f0108 eye level, D:f0053 aerial) - a touch warmer and duller than the neutral the model was using; one giant egg boulder for the body, sphere head, four smaller boulders as arms/legs, two small ears. This is what students call the Warren Bear. Low-poly: 8-10 smooth grey spheres/ovoids stacked into a seated teddy bear.

landmarks.name: La Jolla Project (Stonehenge)
landmarks.description: Richard Fleischner's 71 blocks of pink and grey granite scattered across the Revelle College lawn south of Galbraith Hall, some stacked into post-and-lintel doorways, arches, and benches up to ~2.4 m tall — hence the 'Stonehenge' nickname. Low-poly: a dozen clusters of rectangular blocks, alternating warm pink-beige and cool grey granite, on flat green grass.

landmarks.name: Triton Statue
landmarks.description: Manuelita Brown's bronze King Triton on the plaza at the east entrance of Price Center, muscular merman rising from a wave, trident in hand, on a low stone base. Measured D:f0026 (and D:f0128 on the King Triton at the amphitheatre base, #3f4245): the patina reads dark blue-black, not brown-green. Photo spot for grads. Low-poly: dark bronze torso with raised trident, fish-tail base merging into a wave wedge, grey plinth.

landmarks.name: READ/WRITE/THINK/DREAM
landmarks.description: John Baldessari's artwork forming the main east entrance of Geisel Library: a row of tall glass doors and windows in saturated primary colors (red, blue, yellow, green panes) with the words READ, WRITE, THINK, DREAM, plus large photographic panels inside. Low-poly: the library's ground-level entry wall as a strip of vivid colored glass rectangles under the concrete tower.

landmarks.name: Geisel Library
landmarks.description: The campus icon: an 8-level brutalist 'lantern' — a concrete pedestal with four massive splayed diagonal piers holding five progressively larger-then-smaller glass floors, widest in the middle, like a spaceship or tree canopy. Raw grey concrete piers, dark tinted glass bands with narrow concrete floor slabs. Low-poly: stepped stack of square glass floors (widths ~small/large/largest/large/small) on 4 angled concrete legs.

landmarks.name: Vices and Virtues
landmarks.description: Bruce Nauman's band of 2.1 m tall neon words wrapping the top parapet of the Powell Structural Systems Laboratory (crown sits ~25 m up): seven vices superimposed on seven virtues (FAITH/LUST, HOPE/ENVY...) flashing in alternating neon colors. Measured D:f0033, which corrects two things: the host is a plain GREY board-formed concrete box, not an oxblood one, and the crown is an OPEN OXIDE-RED steel frame - an airy lattice you can see sky through, carrying the tubes and running down the building's corners as red columns. The letters are hot pink-red and mint green (daylight readings; at night they are far brighter). NOT YET RENDERED by campus-landmarks.js - the grey box belongs to campus-facades.json, and the red crown + letter band is future work. Low-poly when built: an open red steel frame band around the parapet with a glowing letter strip inside it.

landmarks.name: Two Running Violet V Forms
landmarks.description: Robert Irwin's two V-shaped runs of blue-violet plastic-coated chain-link fence held ~7.6 m in the air on slim stainless steel poles, threading between eucalyptus trunks in the grove west of Library Walk. Translucent purple-blue shimmer against the trees. Low-poly: two long thin semi-transparent violet ribbons in a shallow V plan, on skinny silver posts among eucalyptus.

landmarks.name: What Hath God Wrought
landmarks.description: Mark Bradford's 199 ft white steel pole — the tallest structure on campus — rising from Revelle College plaza, topped with a light that blinks 'What hath God wrought' in Morse code at night. Looks like an impossibly tall slender flagpole. Low-poly: a single thin white tapering cylinder with a small blinking white light cap.

landmarks.name: KAHNOP - TO TELL A STORY
landmarks.description: Ann Hamilton's ~240 m long granite walkway east of Pepper Canyon, on the route from the trolley station into campus, its pale grey stone pavers carved with raised lines of text (Kumeyaay and English words). Low-poly: a flat light-grey stone ribbon path with subtle darker text striping.

landmarks.name: Theodor Seuss Geisel Memorial (Dr. Seuss statue)
landmarks.description: Bronze of Dr. Seuss seated at his drafting desk with a 2 m Cat in the Hat standing beside him, on the terrace just west of the Geisel Library entrance. Dark brown bronze on a low grey plinth. Low-poly: seated figure at a small desk plus a tall thin cat figure with stovepipe hat, all one bronze color.

landmarks.name: Green Table
landmarks.description: Jenny Holzer's leaf-green granite picnic table and benches engraved with texts, in a grove near Peterson Hall on Ridge Walk. Low-poly: a simple picnic table, solid muted green stone.

landmarks.name: Revelle Plaza Fountain
landmarks.description: The centrepiece of Revelle Plaza, and the thing the walk aims at once it leaves Argo: a low ring basin about 8 m across with a single white aerating jet standing in the middle of it, and the tall US flagpole a dozen metres off its north side. Measured W:f0035 (and corroborated W:f0034, W:f0036): the basin is BLACK - a charcoal basalt that samples #151217 raw in the frame, which is the darkest thing on the plaza and the reason the fountain reads as a hole in the concrete rather than an ornament. The rendered #3a3437 is that reading lifted to daylight, a very dark warm charcoal rather than the literal near-black. The jet samples #a5b1b6 backlit and is rendered as lifted white foam - a single column that flares as it rises, not a fan of nozzles. Position is the surveyed OSM point 'Revelle Plaza Fountain' inside the plaza polygon both the router and the walk cross. The flagpole stand-off is parallax between W:f0034 and W:f0035, which puts it 12-17 m from the basin on the side away from the cafe umbrellas; the flag's own red/white/blue are the canonical US flag colours, NOT measurements - at this distance the flag is a handful of sky-mixed pixels. Low-poly: charcoal rim cylinder, dark water disc, one flaring foam cone, white pole with a small flag box.

landmarks.name: Pergola Swings (Ridge Walk at Muir Field)
landmarks.description: One of a pair of identical rest stations the walk passes: a long black steel post-and-beam trellis with a flat roof of pale timber slats, three hanging bench swings on rods under it and fixed grey benches alongside. Measured W:f0013-f0014, where the run stands at the edge of the mown Muir field with the walk on its other side. Every reading in those frames is against the sun, so the steel samples #0c090a to #2f3036 and the slats read as silhouette: the frame black #3a3634 and the lit timber #c9c2b2 are the daylight values, and the benches #8a8378 with them. Placed on the east side of Ridge Walk at the field's edge, beside the route between Muir and Peterson. Low-poly: two rows of posts, two beams, a rack of slats, three swing seats on rods, two fixed benches.

landmarks.name: Pergola Swings (Revelle Walk)
landmarks.description: The second station of the same furniture family, on the Revelle stretch of the walk north of Bonner Hall. Measured W:f0026 (seen up the walk) and W:f0027 (standing in it, a swing seat hanging on its rods a metre from the lens). Same black steel frame, same pale slat roof, same grey benches as the Muir station - which is the point: it is a repeat, and repeats are what make a campus legible. It sits in the planted median between the bike lane and the pedestrian walk, so the route passes within a few metres of it. The colours are the Muir station's daylight values; both frames here are backlit too.

landmarks.name: Mayer/Bonner Folded-Plate Canopy
landmarks.description: The Revelle silhouette, and the one piece of building shape on this walk that a flat wall cannot fake: a continuous eave of literal triangular concrete prisms - a folded plate - running the length of the Mayer and Bonner arcade on slender round columns, cream #d8d4c6. Measured W:f0022-f0023, where the prisms are the whole top-right of the frame; both readings are of the shaded underside (#4a4a3b, #585351) so the cream is the daylight value. The line it runs along is not stored here: the builder takes the WEST edge of each host's own footprint out of campus-3d.json, so the canopy stays welded to the buildings if the massing ever moves. The two hosts present one unbroken west face about 160 m long, which is the whole east side of the Revelle stretch the route walks. Low-poly: one instanced prism per 2.4 m of run with a column every 4.8 m.

landmarks.name: Sun God Lawn reference - Untitled (Asher fountain)
landmarks.description: Michael Asher's granite drinking fountain shaped like a commercial office fountain, oddly alone on the plaza north of Price Center. Speckled grey granite box. Low-poly: a knee-high grey rectangular block with a basin notch.
